brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A snow-white wild plant infusion listed as a speciality of Shangri-La, also called earth tea and Taibai tea. It is described as growing on snow mountains at 3000 to 5000 metres and as impossible to cultivate.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Accounts of it disagree: the white hollow strands fit the wild snow tea of the region, yet the same name is also attached to a plucked and pan-fried green leaf tea said to have been rated a quality tea in Yunnan in 1989. Little more is settled.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_dry: Slender, hollow, greyish-white tubes 3 to 7 cm long, single or with 2 or 3 branches, likened to white chrysanthemum petals.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: Described as lightly fragrant and slightly bitter with a sweet return.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
